en.title: Farewell to “topology hell” and “texture duds”: Tencent Hunyuan launches Hy3D 3.6, with native 3D generation taking direct aim at professional pipeline pain points

en.title: Can general-purpose large models "break through" physical AI? He Xiaopeng offers a sobering answer: the constraints of the physical world can't be papered over with parameters
en.reason: At XPeng Tech Day, XPeng Group chairman and CEO He Xiaopeng argued that physical-world AI faces stricter constraints than the digital world, and general large models alone cannot solve all physical AI challenges, dampening the parameter race.

en.title: Former OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy proposed the "LLM Wiki" concept on GitHub in April, arguing that unstructured documents should be compiled into a reasoning-ready knowledge network to address the inefficiency of repeated retrieval and reasoning in large models.
en.reason: Andrej Karpathy’s April GitHub LLM Wiki concept, which drew over 10,000 stars, became an enterprise product eight months later when Haimayun launched lumimax, supporting tens of millions of characters of multimodal ingestion and DEN-based cross-document knowledge graphs with conflict detection.

en.title:
Looks like Seedance is about to get steamrolled — MAGI-2-preview now runs on 96GB of VRAM. The community's NVFP4 quant version:
· Compresses only the expert weights, shrinking the transformer from 228GB to 71.8GB
· 96GB VRAM plus 64GB RAM, with the entire model loaded into VRAM and no offload support
· 4-bit only saves VRAM and load time (60.5s → 9.5s); per-step speed is essentially unchanged
· In ComfyUI, install the author's node pack and use the built-in Load…
en.summary:
Seedance is about to get crushed into the ground.
MAGI-2-preview can now run on 96GB of VRAM.

The community's NVFP4 quantized version:
- Compresses only the expert weights, shrinking the transformer from 228GB to 71.8GB.
- With 96GB of VRAM and 64GB of RAM, the entire model fits in VRAM; offload is not supported.
- 4-bit only saves VRAM and loading time (60.5s → 9.5s); per-step speed is basically unchanged.
- Install the author's node package in ComfyUI and load it directly with the built-in Load Diffusion Model.

That said, there is still a lot of room to improve the speed. For a 10s video on a single RTX PRO 6000: 540p, 100 steps, 32 min 47 sec; 1080p (3+5 steps), 18 min 31…
en.reason: Community NVFP4 quantization cuts MAGI-2-preview's transformer from 228GB to 71.8GB, letting 96GB VRAM plus 64GB RAM hold it without offload and load in 9.5s instead of 60.5s, though a 10s 540p 100-step run still takes 32m47s on RTX PRO 6000.

en.title: Your AI assistant can write code and hold a conversation, but ask it to batch-edit 50 images or convert a pile of ebooks, and it’ll likely be stumped.
en.summary:
Your AI assistant can write code and hold a conversation, but ask it to batch-retouch 50 images or convert a pile of ebooks from one format to another, and it will mostly just stare at you. The reason is simple: these programs were designed from day one for a human with a mouse, and AI has no way in.

I usually write about markets, but here's an open-source detour. One project aims to fill that gap: CLI-Anything, No. 3 on GitHub's daily trending list today, up 668 stars in a single day, with more than 66,000 total. I went through the README and the repo, and read the discussion on X too — here's my take.

1. What problem does it solve

Professional software's entry points are windows, buttons and menus, and its default user is a person sitting in front of a screen. An agent (an AI that can call tools and do work on its own) trying to use them used to imitate a human: take a screenshot, find the button in the image, click it. It works, but it's fragile…
en.reason: Open-source project CLI-Anything, ranked 3rd on GitHub's daily chart with 668 stars added in a single day and over 66,000 total, addresses how AI agents can operate professional software like batch-editing 50 images or converting ebooks without screenshot-and-click workarounds.

stories.title: 卧槽，OpenAI 联合创始人 Andrej Karpathy 刚刚分享了自己的屏幕，毫无保留地展示了他每天如何与大型 AI 模型协作。 整整 70 分钟。没有花哨的 PowerPoint 演示，没有空洞的理论。只有一位跻身全球最顶尖 1% AI 用户行列的人，如何与 AI 协作的真实演示。 而最令人惊讶的是，他的方法竟然如此简单。 一切都归结为四个步骤： 提示词 → 上下文 → 工具 → 工作流。 这就是那些真正把 AI 用到极致的…

en.title: Holy crap, OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy just shared his screen, giving a completely unfiltered look at how he works with large AI models every day.
en.summary:
Wow—OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy just shared his screen, holding nothing back about how he collaborates with large AI models every day.

A full 70 minutes. No fancy PowerPoint decks, no empty theory. Just a real demonstration of how someone in the world’s top 1% of AI users works with AI.

And the most surprising part: his method is incredibly simple.

It all comes down to four steps:

Prompt → Context → Tools → Workflow.

That’s how people who truly get the most out of AI actually work.

Here’s something many people need to hear:

Most people hit a wall with AI not because the models aren’t powerful enough, but because they make things too complicated.…
en.reason: OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy's 70-minute unscripted screen recording shows how he collaborates with large AI models through four steps—prompt, context, tools, workflow—and argues most users hit bottlenecks by overcomplicating their approach rather than lacking model power.

en.title: Holy crap, OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy just shared his screen, giving a completely unfiltered look at how he works with large AI models every day.
en.summary:
Wow—OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy just shared his screen, holding nothing back about how he collaborates with large AI models every day.

A full 70 minutes. No fancy PowerPoint decks, no empty theory. Just a real demonstration of how someone in the world’s top 1% of AI users works with AI.

And the most surprising part: his method is incredibly simple.

It all comes down to four steps:

Prompt → Context → Tools → Workflow.

That’s how people who truly get the most out of AI actually work.

Here’s something many people need to hear:

Most people hit a wall with AI not because the models aren’t powerful enough, but because they make things too complicated.…

Title: Woman Evicted After Landlord’s AI Assistant Allegedly Said She Could Delay $3,934 Rent Payment
Published Time: 2026-11-19T17:30:00-08:00
Emails reviewed by WRAL appeared to accept Laura Mack’s proposed November 30 payment date, while Colony Townhome Apartments has not confirmed her account of the exchange.
A North Carolina woman lost her home after an email appearing to come from her apartment complex approved a later deadline for paying nearly $4,000 in overdue rent. She says the message
sources.recommend_reason_zh: 租客Laura Mack称房东AI助手Olivia邮件同意她11月30日付$3,934.17欠租，但她在11月19日仍被驱逐，引发自动化承诺责任追问。

en.title: Landlord's AI assistant told a woman she could delay her rent payment — then she was deported

stories.title: 十年：谷歌更新 SRE 著作，拥抱 AI 时代

sources.title: 十年：谷歌更新 SRE 著作，拥抱 AI 时代
sources.title_zh: 十年：谷歌更新 SRE 著作，拥抱 AI 时代
sources.title_original: 十年：谷歌更新 SRE 著作，拥抱 AI 时代
sources.summary:
谷歌官宣重写经典 SRE 著作并发布第二版。
谷歌官宣重写经典 SRE 著作并发布第二版。
本文字数：2265 字
阅读完需：约 7 分钟
谷歌重写《Site Reliability Engineering》第二版，十年后系统性更新SRE方法论，适配云原生、平台工程与AI负载场景。
保留“以软件工程驱动运维”的核心范式，强化分布式系统可靠性治理；新增对动态边界、复杂依赖与高破坏性故障模式的应对策略；延续SLO、错误预算、自动化减负等经典实践并重新语境化。
适合SRE工程师、平台工程负责人、云原生架构师阅读。
谷歌宣布对其开创性著作 《Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems》（网站可靠性工程：谷歌如何运行生产系统） 进行了彻底重写，推出了第二版，距该书首版问世已有十年。本书更新了网站可靠性工程（SRE）的理念，覆盖现代云架构、平台工程和 AI 工作负载，同时保留了将软件工程技术应用于运维工作的原始核心理念。
新版本由谷歌 SRE 项目经理 Betsy Beyer 和软件工程师 David Huska
sources.recommend_reason_zh: 谷歌重写《Site Reliability Engineering》第二版，距首版十年，由 Betsy Beyer 和 David Huska 发布，新增 AI 工作负载、以用户为中心的多层 SLO 与 GPU/TPU 集群可靠性等内容。

en.title: A decade on: Google updates its SRE book to embrace the AI era
en.summary:
Google has officially announced a rewritten second edition of its classic SRE book.

Google has officially announced a rewritten second edition of its classic SRE book.

Word count: 2,265 words
Reading time: about 7 minutes

Google has rewritten Site Reliability Engineering for a second edition, systematically updating its SRE methodology a decade later to fit cloud-native, platform engineering and AI workload scenarios.

It retains the core paradigm of "driving operations with software engineering" and strengthens reliability governance for distributed systems; adds strategies for handling dynamic boundaries, complex dependencies and highly destructive failure modes; and carries forward classic practices such as SLOs, error budgets and automation-driven toil reduction, recontextualized for today.

Suited to SRE engineers, platform engineering leads and cloud-native architects.

Google announced a thorough rewrite of its groundbreaking book Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems, releasing a second edition ten years after the first. The book updates site reliability engineering (SRE) ideas to cover modern cloud architecture, platform engineering and AI workloads, while preserving the original core idea of applying software engineering techniques to operations work.

The new edition is by Google SRE program manager Betsy Beyer and software engineer David Huska
en.reason: Google has fully rewritten *Site Reliability Engineering* for a second edition ten years after the original, with Betsy Beyer and David Huska adding AI workloads and GPU/TPU cluster reliability while retaining SLOs, error budgets and software-engineering-driven operations across cloud-native and platform engineering.

体验了一下字节的 Personal Agent「小豆」，感觉它可能会成为国内第一批真正走向大众的个人智能体产品。

第一眼看到界面，差点以为打开了 Muse，哈哈哈。整体交互也有点 Manus 旗下 Cue 的影子。

简单说一下今天的体验。

01｜日常生活服务

测试了附近餐厅推荐、高铁票查询等功能。

只需要说一句话，它就能帮你筛选附近餐厅，整理距离、人均消费、口碑，也能通过高铁管家查询车次、票价和余票。

目前体验下来，几次普通查询都是免费的，产品内部也已经有了独立的额度消耗明细。

en.summary:
Tried ByteDance's Personal Agent Xiaodou, and I suspect it could be among the first personal agent products in China to genuinely reach a mainstream audience.

At first glance I almost thought I'd opened Muse, haha. The overall interaction also carries a hint of Cue, the product from Manus.

A quick rundown of today's experience.

01 | Everyday life services

I tested nearby restaurant recommendations, high-speed rail ticket lookups and similar features.

With a single sentence, it screens nearby restaurants for you and lays out distance, per-person spend and reputation, and it can look up train numbers, fares and remaining seats through Gaotie Guanji.

So far, several ordinary queries have been free, and the product already has its own separate breakdown of credit usage.

02 | The Douyin ecosystem may be the biggest highlight

What surprised me most wasn't the task execution, but the integration with Douyin.

sources.summary:
本文字数：2382 字
阅读完需：约 8 分钟
AI正从辅助工具演进为可承担任务的智能体，企业面临的核心挑战转向任务适配、结果验收与权限成本风险管控。
AICon 2026 北京站聚焦真实生产环境中的 AI 工程实践，覆盖 Agent 工程、评测安全、自进化系统等 13 大专题；华映资本李岩将剖析模型快速迭代下需持续积累的系统能力。

en.title: If you're getting ready to enter computer graphics now, are you looking at a shrinking career path—or a chance for AI to reshuffle the deck?
en.summary:
If you're about to enter computer graphics now, are you looking at a shrinking career path, or an opportunity to be reshuffled by AI?

My view is blunt: by 2026, prioritize going deep on AI, because many of the practices graphics has built up over the years don't line up with the direction the bitter lesson points to.

Graphics research will sooner or later be substantially rewritten by AI—calling it a thorough reshaping wouldn't be an exaggeration.

When I first got into rendering, one question kept coming back to me: in what everyone calls "physically real," which part is actually physics, and which part is actually real?

Look closely and you'll see the graphics pipeline is stuffed with human-added bias.

Why are material formulas modeled this way? Why, beyond brdf, bsdf and bssdf, are there so many other bxdfs?

Why does hair need a separate model of its own?

Blinn-P…
Look
en.reason: Graphics pipelines are packed with human-added bias—separate BRDF, BSDF and BxDF models, plus a dedicated hair model—and the author argues that by 2026 learners should prioritize AI, since these practices will be heavily rewritten or even reshaped.

stories.title: 「AI 会不会毁灭人类」这个问题，卡巴斯基的 CEO 给了个更现实的答案：短期不会，但它正在变成黑客手里的工具。 尤金·卡巴斯基（Eugene Kaspersky）在接受采访时说，AI 在短期内不会像科幻电影那样统治人类，可它带来的安全风险已经远超他此前的预期。 最核心的变化是「智能体」。过去语言模型只是个会聊天的框，只要不接触关键开关，就出不了大事；现在攻击者可以把权限交给 AI 智能体，让它自己去执行一连串攻击动作，传统防御体系会…

en.title: AI in children's education is set to be a major monetization opportunity in the coming years.
en.summary:
AI + children's education is shaping up to be one of the biggest monetization opportunities of the next few years.

Plenty of people want in but get stuck because they don't have an engineering team. The thing is, GitHub already has a wealth of open-source projects that permit commercial use.

I've picked out 10 of the best — bookmark these: 👇👇👇

1. Primer: a Socratic AI learning companion
Rather than handing over answers, it guides kids to think by asking follow-up questions (e.g., "What color is the sky at sunset? Why do you think that is?").
Runs offline, with data stored locally.
Monetization: philosophy for kids, at-home AI tutoring, custom builds for private schools.

https://t.co/lYcQY6QfIX

2. Math-To-Manim: AI-generated math and physics animations
Combines Manim, Blender and more to turn abstract concepts into animated teaching videos.
Monetization: math education media, early-learning videos for kids, teaching anim…

en.title: AI in children's education is set to be a major monetization opportunity in the coming years.
en.summary:
AI + children's education is shaping up to be one of the biggest monetization opportunities of the next few years.

Plenty of people want in but get stuck because they don't have an engineering team. The thing is, GitHub already has a wealth of open-source projects that permit commercial use.

I've picked out 10 of the best — bookmark these: 👇👇👇

1. Primer: a Socratic AI learning companion
Rather than handing over answers, it guides kids to think by asking follow-up questions (e.g., "What color is the sky at sunset? Why do you think that is?").
Runs offline, with data stored locally.
Monetization: philosophy for kids, at-home AI tutoring, custom builds for private schools.

https://t.co/lYcQY6QfIX

2. Math-To-Manim: AI-generated math and physics animations
Combines Manim, Blender and more to turn abstract concepts into animated teaching videos.
Monetization: math education media, early-learning videos for kids, teaching anim…

en.title: Stock falls below IPO price, users complain, founder cashes out — Anthropic CEO responds late at night: I never wanted AI to rule humanity
en.reason: Anthropic’s stock fell below its IPO price within a week as seven cofounders sold shares, prompting CEO Dario Amodei’s November 25 X post denying he advocates handing human free will to AI and distinguishing task automation from social governance.

en.title:
Nov 27 AI Daily | Compute compliance tightens as quotas and Agent infrastructure accelerate
01 NVIDIA reportedly indefinitely suspends AI server chip shipments to four Southeast Asian countries
According to The Wall Street Journal and TechCrunch, NVIDIA has told Dell, Super Micro, and other manufacturing partners to indefinitely suspend AI server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia to verify whether regional partners comply with US export control requirements.
en.reason: NVIDIA has reportedly told Dell and Super Micro to indefinitely halt AI server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia pending an export-control compliance review, following a US Commerce Department crackdown on Chinese remote access to chips via Southeast Asian data centers—a channel the Institute for Progress estimated supplied about 24% of China's AI compute.

en.reason: DoorDash precomputes 90-day purchase cycles with batch LLM inference and deterministic validation to cut grocery reorder latency from 16 seconds to 2 seconds, while real-time catalog parsing and an editable shopping interface keep selections current and reportedly double shopping-list views and lift order conversion about 34%.

What scar

en.title: Without AI, I Never Realized How Much My Colleagues Struggle
en.summary:
I'm a Java backend developer. In the past, when I estimated work for a feature, I rarely counted visuals, animation, and sound effects as a separate task—to me, that was just "polish it up after the page is done." So let me be honest: I never really knew what my frontend and product-ops colleagues were busy with all day.

Then AI made writing code easier, and I did all of that work myself, from scratch. The biggest takeaway wasn't "my colleagues have it rough"—it was that I finally understood who had been making all those tiny decisions for me.

It started with something trivial: I wanted to know how many days were left until my next vacation. I use an iPhone, and the only way to get that number was to download some third-party app from the store—burn a home screen slot and grant notification permissions for a single number, then gamble on whether it had updated this year's holidays. So I just built one myself: open it and there's the countdown. It later grew into four entries—countdown, water, slacking off, check-in.

Image: the home page serves just one number.

Features can be added slowly, but one rule I held from the start: that number on the home page cannot move. No matter how much gets added later, it stays right where it is.

This used to not count as work in my eyes—"isn't it just putting a number—
en.reason: A Java backend developer used AI to build a four-entry mini-program—countdown, water, slacking and check-in—and found that its homepage’s 1,900-line script, 26 animation keyframes and 11 sound effects carry front-end judgment and responsibility.

最近有很多朋友来问我如何从0到1造出一个benchmark，特别是如何找到灵感和方向并迈出第一步。我的回答是，造好一道高质量的题比上来就造一个bench会更有价值。另外，不管你是学传统理工科的同学，还是做AI领域其他方向的同学，造benchmark题目最好的原材料，其实都藏在你自己使用Claude code/Codex等agent的轨迹里面。对于想入坑benchmark的同学，我将用最简单最不绕弯子的话告诉你，如何从你的agent使用轨迹中造出一道terminal-bench级别的benchmark题目。
我们做benchmark的目的是为了定义那些有价值且模型目前还做不好的问题。如果模型在某些问题上的表现与人类专家的预期还有gap，那么就有造bench的空间，如果这个gap越大、问题越有经济价值，这个bench就越值得造。
想必你已经回忆起很多这种“gap”出现的场景——比如你让AI帮你做科研任务的时候，它在你的工作区里面拉了一坨大的，然后你不断给AI纠偏，在一个session里面交

en.title: In the simplest, most direct terms: how to build a terminal-bench-level benchmark task from your agent usage traces.
en.summary:
Survival Guide for the Great Bench Era
Survival Guide for the Great Bench Era
Survival Guide for the Great Bench Era
See the latest updates and join the conversation
Recently, many friends have asked me how to build a benchmark from 0 to 1—especially how to find inspiration and direction and take the first step. My answer is that writing one high-quality question is more valuable than building a whole bench right away. And whether you're in a traditional STEM field or another area of AI, the best raw material for benchmark questions is actually hidden in your own traces of using agents like Claude code/Codex. For anyone looking to get into benchmarks, I'll explain in the simplest, most direct terms how to turn your agent usage traces into a terminal-bench-level benchmark question.
The goal of building benchmarks is to define problems that are valuable and that models still can't do well. If model performance still has a gap versus what human experts expect, there's room to build a bench; the larger the gap and the more economically valuable the problem, the more worth building the bench.
You've probably recalled many situations where this “gap” appears—for example, when you ask AI to help with a research task and it makes a huge mess in your workspace, then you keep correcting the AI, and within a single session...
en.reason: Claude Code or Codex agent traces can supply raw material for a terminal-bench-level task: find a case the model still fails after over 100 interaction rounds, cut it, build a Docker environment with verifier and oracle, then run it.

sources.recommend_reason_zh: 文章从普通使用者的困惑出发，系统拆解 LLM、Token、Context Window、Transformer、Attention、Embedding 到模型训练、微调和量化，并区分 AI 技术领域与 ChatGPT、Gemini、Claude 等产品。

en.title: Stop just using AI!
en.reason: A beginner's guide that moves from chatting with ChatGPT and DeepSeek to explaining what an LLM actually is, covering Token, Context Window, Transformer, Attention, Embedding, plus model training, fine-tuning and quantization, and separating the AI field from products like ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude.

en.reason: NEURA Robotics' MoU with Aragón's government and Costa Group targets a Spanish robot training gym by mid-2027, backed by tens of millions of euros, where firms train robots on real tasks and license skills via Neuraverse.

sources.title_original: 我写的 12 个 AI Skill，三个月后 8 个在吃空饷
sources.recommend_reason_zh: 作者三个月写的12个AI Skill只剩4个在跑，提交30次、最上心的度量岗死得最早，5个Skill同在9月21日停更，文中附盘点脚本和5条裁人标准，点明没有真值、靠人记着触发的Skill注定吃空饷。

en.title: I Wrote 12 AI Skills. Three Months Later, 8 of Them Are Collecting Paychecks for Doing Nothing
en.reason: Over three months the author built 12 AI Skills but only 4 remain active—defect closure, pixel restoration, code discipline and campaign page development—while 8 stalled, including the most-committed metrics Skill and five that stopped updating on 21 September, with the piece tracing the causes (no ground truth, human-remembered triggers, upkeep exceeding payoff) and offering an inventory script plus 5 criteria for retiring a Skill.
